text: BRD Program v5, BRD Epic 1 v5, BRD Epic 2 v3 and BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 are taken as the approved business baseline for this PRD even though none of them carries a status field or an approval record, so the PRD is issued as Draft with an empty approval table and the requirements approval gate stays open.
why: No BRD in the set has a status row or a governance decision row (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-11), and the realignment run does not stop for a missing approval.
read: The four BRDs, at the versions read for this work package, are the baseline; the PRD approval is pending.
applied_in: Section 1 document control, section 13 approval table
confirm: Product Owner and FDA at the requirements approval gate
impact: The PRD is a Draft baseline; no story is blocked because the story set already exists.

text: There is no predecessor PRD for rwb-agent in the PRD folder, so this file is version 1 of the P10 family and no earlier PRD content is preserved.
why: The PRD folder holds P1, P2 and P4 at version 1 and no P10 file, and Story Template and Rules R8.2 takes the next version as the highest existing version plus one.
read: Version 1 is the correct version number for a new family member.
impact: A later PRD of this family continues at version 2.

text: The product baseline of this PRD is BRD Program v5 sections 5.3, 5.5, 5.7 and 6, BRD Epic 1 v5 section 3.9, BRD Epic 2 v3 section 3.10, BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 sections 8.1 and 8.6, FSD P10 Agent runtime v3, Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, the Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 and the Ownership Map v1; the Story Template and Rules v1 supplies the precedence rule, the DP table and the R9 placeholder.
why: The source set names several versions of each family, and the run reads the highest version of each; Architecture v5 wins where the sources disagree (R-PREC rule 1).
read: FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 dated 15 November 2026 is the functional detail; Arch v5 is the constraint.
impact: A later BRD or FSD version re-baselines the FR and NFR tables.

text: The business requirements of rwb-agent are taken from four carrier sections of the BRD because the BRD gives P10 no requirement section of its own: REQ-CWC-017 to REQ-CWC-019 from section 5.3, REQ-DCM-005, REQ-DCM-006 and REQ-DCM-011 from section 5.5, REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-005 and REQ-APD-005 from section 5.7, REQ-ACA-005, REQ-ACA-010 and REQ-CHO-006 from sections 5.4 and 5.3, REQ-DVH-001 from section 5.15, and BR-015, BR-081 and BR-084 from the epics 3 to 8 BRD.
why: BRD Program v5 section 12 gap CG-8 and its section 11 note state that P10 has no requirement section and that the agent and model duties are carried inside sections 5.3, 5.5, 5.7 and 6.9.
read: The carrier sections are the requirement source; the BRD IDs are copied unchanged and none is renumbered.
confirm: Product owner with the centre of excellence
impact: If the BRD assigns a further agent duty to P10 in its next version, a capability and a requirement are added.

text: Architecture v5 wins on the data lake: the agent dashboard is served on screen SCR-46 from the service's own daily per-agent measures and from the read model of rwb-reporting, and no lake file, lake row, Power BI data set or lake delivery exists.
why: Architecture v5 slides 7, 8, 13 and 37, ADR-018 and DP-17 remove the data lake and the Power BI connection, while FSD P10 v3 A2.6 still builds the dashboard through a lake write (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-1).
read: Precedence R-PREC rule 1 puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the FSD; the loser is recorded as a gap and as this assumption.
applied_in: Section 2.2, section 5.1, section 6 FR-P10-016 and FR-P10-017, section 9, section 10
impact: FSD P10 v3 A2.6 and BRD Epic 1 v5 RWB-E1-063 need the same correction in their next versions.

text: The daily per-agent measure the FSD asserts is read as a projection over the agent run record for the business date, one row per agent and policy and prompt version, idempotent on the date; its physical name, its columns and its retention are the technical specification's.
why: The FSD names agent_run_daily in two acceptance criteria and the Logical Data Model v8 and the Ownership Map list eight agent tables without it (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-2).
read: A projection holds the same content as the table the FSD describes, so the acceptance criteria can be met without a ninth table.
applied_in: Section 5.1, section 6 FR-P10-016 and FR-P10-017, section 8
impact: If the technical specification needs a stored table, one table is added to the P10 schema and to the LDM.

text: Because the FSD P10 requirement table is empty, every functional requirement of this PRD is mapped to the FSD section and to the acceptance criteria it serves, and to the feature code FEAT-AGT-nn where the feature overview carries one; no FSD requirement ID is invented.
why: FSD P10 v3 section Requirements served has a heading and no row (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-7).
read: A section plus an acceptance criterion identifies the source as well as a requirement key would.
applied_in: Section 1.4, section 6 FSD source column, section 11.1
impact: When the FSD fills its requirement table, each FR gains a requirement key and the mapping is reloaded.

text: Only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views; every case fact a run needs is read through the rwb-source-data tool contract, one hop with a 2 s budget, every extracted document field through the rwb-document tool contract, and the rwb_agent login holds no grant on the recovery schema and no grant on another rwb_* schema.
why: Architecture v5 slides 9, 16, 29 and 35, ADR-010 and DP-05 reserve the views to rwb-source-data, while FSD P10 v3 names ACE as an integration point of four features (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-3).
read: The FSD sentences that name ACE are the legacy wording of how the facts were reached; in the target they arrive through the owner's tool contract.
applied_in: Section 2.3, section 2.4, section 6 FR-P10-025, section 8, section 9
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data owner
impact: A read grant on the views would break the service boundary and the architecture test.

text: The tool gateway is read-only for wave 1 and wave 2 and the allowed tool list can only narrow what a run may read; no agent writes to a case, a queue, a task, a deviation, a treatment or another service, and a write tool is an open question and not a requirement of this PRD.
why: Architecture v5 slide 16 states read-only calls for the agent and slide 35 states that AI suggests and never decides, while FSD P10 v3 A2.2 tests an allowed action list and BRD REQ-CWC-018 speaks of an agent writing to a queue (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-13).
read: The read-only tool gateway is the narrower and safer reading, and it is the one the architecture states.
applied_in: Section 2.2, section 6 FR-P10-025, section 11 AC-P10-016, section 12 Q-P10-06
confirm: Solution architect with the model risk officer
impact: A decision to allow a write tool adds a capability, a limit and a security review to this PRD.

text: The service calls an approved model endpoint through the model gateway and hosts, trains and fine-tunes no model; the model code and version, the price per token and the daily cost cap are policy rows and not a model registry.
why: No source in the set describes model training, tuning or a model registry; Architecture v5 slide 35 and NFR-048 describe an approved external endpoint on a private endpoint.
read: The Enterprise AI endpoint (INT-23) is the only model runtime this service uses.
impact: A model registry need would become a separate capability with its own requirements.

text: Every target the source does not state is written with the R9 placeholder and carried as an open question; the only numeric targets stated in the source set are the 60 second agent target and the fallback rate below 10 percent, and both are carried as stated.
why: BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 KPI-012 and Q-026 leave the agent measures with no target, Q-014 leaves the autonomy evidence and threshold open, and DL11 leaves the non-functional values open (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-8).
read: The BRD and FSD statements are copied, and nothing is invented to fill a gap.
impact: The targets arrive with DL11 and Q-P10-01 and Q-P10-02 and re-baseline the NFR table.

text: The run, the guardrail result, the feedback, the sample, the evaluation and the alert are retained for the period set for them, are answerable to audit before a purge and are never removed silently; the period is written with the R9 placeholder until DL26 is answered.
why: No source states a retention period for any agent entity and DL26 is open for every data product and document type (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-9).
read: The record proves what an answer was, so it is retained at least as long as the decision it supports.
impact: A purge set before the case closes destroys the evidence of an answer.

text: The deviation screening feature FEAT-AGT-08 is read as a shadow run whose proposal is acted on only when the policy row is at L1; the main criterion of A2.8 that stores mode SHADOW and creates no deviation record is the shadow behaviour, and the L1 behaviour is the same run with the proposal handed to rwb-deviation.
why: The A2.8 heading says at L1 while its main criterion stores mode SHADOW and asserts that no deviation record exists, and the feature table of A1.2 first places FEAT-AGT-08 in E2.
read: One code path with the mode read from the policy row serves both, which is how the intake agent is described in A2.7.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P10-004, section 6 FR-P10-007 and FR-P10-013, section 10
impact: If the two are separate code paths, the story set splits and the mode row is read in two places.

text: The cost cap and drift notifications to the holders of the centre-of-excellence and model-risk roles use the ACE notification path (NSS and LINE OA) and need no build in this service.
why: FSD P10 v3 AC-ALT-P10-006-01 sends MSG-P10-004 through the notification path, and the ACE common module owns that path with no P10 build.
read: The alert row is the service's evidence; the delivery is the shared path's, with the unsent state kept when the path is down.
impact: A dedicated channel would be a new integration and a new owner.

text: JOB-15 stays the 01:30 reporting extract of P9 rwb-reporting; rwb-agent runs its own daily aggregation step once per business date after the run record closes, and the per-agent measures are handed to rwb-reporting for the read model so that JOB-15 and the read model carry them.
why: The Ownership Map and Architecture v5 slide 44 give JOB-15 to P9, while FSD P10 v3 fires its dashboard work on the completion of JOB-15 (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-4).
read: The service that owns the run record owns the measure of it, and the reporting service owns the extract and the read model.
confirm: Platform administrator with the rwb-reporting owner
impact: Two schedules touching the same measures need one order; without it the read model shows a partial day.

text: The service base is /api/recovery/agent/v1 behind gateway-bff, and the admin and run operations keep the product names the Ownership Map and the API Specification v4 carry; the exact path spelling is the service contract's and not this PRD's.
why: FSD P10 v3 uses /admin/agent-configs and the shape /agent-runs/{id}, Architecture v5 slide 16 uses /agent-policies (admin), and no source states the P10 base path (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-5).
read: Story Template and Rules DP-13 fixes the base pattern, so only the operation names were in doubt.
impact: A path decision at contract time changes the contract story and the fake, not the product requirement.

text: RWB-E2-028, RWB-E2-029 and RWB-E2-030 are read as the legacy story keys of the feedback, the screening rejection and the legal document pack, even though BRD Epic 2 v3 holds no requirement row for them.
why: FSD P10 v3 cites the three keys and BRD Epic 2 v3 gap CG-B-REQ-BRD-E2-4 records that ten keys, these three among them, have no requirement row (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-12).
read: The split plan holds slices for all three keys, so the story exists even where the epic requirement row does not.
confirm: Product owner with the backlog builder
impact: If the epic BRD drops the keys, the story set keeps them and the trace loses the epic line.

text: The queue write interface and the queue ordering required by REQ-CWC-017 to REQ-CWC-020 belong to P3 rwb-case, and this service supplies only the agent side: the proposal, its reason and its score reach the queue through that owner's contract and in that owner's order.
why: BRD Program v5 section 11 traces REQ-CWC-017 to REQ-CWC-020 to RWB-SVC-P3, and BRD Epic 2 v3 traces RWB-E2-036 to RWB-SVC-P2, so the queue is not a P10 object.
read: A P10 requirement may still state the agent side of the call without owning the queue.
impact: Building a queue write in P10 would duplicate the case service and break the boundary.

text: No BRD requirement ID, requirement text, priority, business owner or epic column is renumbered or reworded by this PRD; every BR ID is copied unchanged from the version read.
why: BRD Program v5 section 10.6 states that no requirement of section 5 changes under D-RCV-60, and Story Template and Rules R8.5 keeps the BR IDs stable.
read: A PRD that renumbered a BR would break the trace of every other service PRD.
impact: None; the IDs are the join key of the whole requirement set.

text: Every date in this PRD is copied unchanged from BRD Program v5 section 8 and from the wave table of section 10.3, and every one is marked tentative; no date is raised as a gap and no date is invented, including for the platform wave.
why: Story Template and Rules U7 and DL48 keep the dates unchanged and tentative, and the wave 0 date is stated only as a month.
read: The release plan of the BRD is the single date source for this PRD.
impact: A date change is a change to the BRD release plan and is picked up on the next version.

text: The service owns the eight agent tables named by the Ownership Map and creates the outbox, inbox, idempotency and local decision-record objects of the platform library in its own schema; it owns no case, document, deviation, treatment, queue or ACE object.
why: The Ownership Map Tables sheet lists eight P10 rows, and DP-09 and DP-03 create the library objects in each service schema.
read: The library objects are platform objects with a per-service copy, not product entities of this PRD.
impact: A product entity missing from the Ownership Map would need a ruling before it is built.

text: The message codes MSG-P10-001 to MSG-P10-008 are referenced with the behaviour the source states and with no invented wording; the wording is taken from the Error and Message Standard at build time, and where the source does not say which service owns a message the PRD leaves that to the screen owner.
why: No source in the set states the wording of the P10 messages (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-6), and the ownership of MSG-P10-007 on a treatment screen is not stated (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-16).
read: Appendix B of the FSD sends every message to the Error and Message Standard, so the code is the requirement and the text is not.
confirm: Business lead with the centre of excellence
impact: A code with no entry in the message standard blocks the story that shows it.

text: Where four FSD features carry the same main success and alternate criteria, the PRD keeps those criteria once as the shared behaviour of the runtime and gives each feature the criterion that shows its own behaviour: the guardrail rejects and falls back, the fallback returns the rule result, the harness scores, and the platform set-up produces the run row and the event.
why: The criteria of A2.1, A2.2, A2.5 and A2.11 are identical in text (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-15), so one criterion cannot accept four features.
read: The FSD repeats its criteria because the four features share one runtime; the feature is told apart by the check, the fallback and the score it produces.
applied_in: Section 11 acceptance criteria and the mapping table
impact: The story set carries one shared criterion set and one feature criterion per story.

text: SCR-46 Agent monitor is described by what it shows and by the filter it applies (agent, policy version, prompt version, business date); its layout, components and states follow the Design System and Component Library and are not fixed by this PRD.
why: The FSD names the screen and no screen specification exists in the source set (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P10-14).
read: The product behaviour of the screen is a requirement; the layout is the design system's.
impact: A screen design decision at story time changes no product requirement.
